name: Adam J. Asis
headline: I architect secure systems.
tagline: Then I teach others to do the same.
thesis: Every AI model and edge device is only as trustworthy as the system around it. I study how to secure the systems that think and act outside the data center.
description: Lectures, notes, research and labs on cybersecurity, with a focus on securing AI and edge computing.

labs.blurb: Security labs, home-lab builds and tools, plus hobby robotics R&D, each with its artifacts and write-up.
labs.card: Personal projects with their development artifacts: links, images, graphics, resources and more.

research.blurb: Long-running security research on AI and the edge, with the evidence and artifacts that connect it to Labs and Lectures.
research.card: Thought experiments and research, with the data and artifacts that connect them to current Labs and Lectures.

journal.blurb: Learning in public: short notes on what I am studying, testing and breaking in security, AI and edge, plus opinions on where the field is heading.
journal.card: Opinion pieces, briefs and general thoughts. Mostly thought leadership, mental exercises and daily musings on the changing landscape of technology.

lectures.blurb: Essays, white papers and case studies. For the Board Room pieces translate security risk for decision-makers; In the Classroom pieces are for students and career changers entering security.
lectures.card: Professional essays, articles and white papers. For the Board Room pieces explain technology for decision-makers; In the Classroom pieces are written for students and new technologists.

library.blurb: The courses, books, tools and labs I am using to learn security, with honest reviews of what was worth the time.
library.card: A curated list of learning materials, tools and content I have used, recommend or reviewed.

contact.blurb: For speaking, advising, collaboration or a conversation about the work.
